countNotes: Counts are entries per SDN asset tag, verified by downloading each .txt and counting non-empty lines on 2026-07-12.

USDT tag (93) breaks down by address format: 78 TRON-format (T...), 8 Ethereum-format (0x...), 7 Bitcoin-format (1.../3...). OFAC tags an address under USDT separately from the chain tag: TRX-vs-USDT list overlap is 0 addresses; ETH-vs-USDT overlap is 4 addresses (case-insensitive comparison).
TRX count (181) includes the 131 ISIS-K TRON addresses added 2026-07-01.

tether.policy: Voluntary OFAC-SDN wallet-freezing policy adopted 2023-12-01, announced 2023-12-09, extending sanctions controls to the secondary market. Before that (Aug 2022) Tether publicly declined to proactively freeze OFAC-sanctioned Tornado Cash addresses absent a specific law-enforcement request.

documentedFreezeEvents.event: Froze 32 addresses holding $873,118.34 linked to terrorism and warfare in Israel and Ukraine, working with Israel's National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing (NBCTF) after the Oct 7 Hamas attack.

Froze approximately $225 million USDT linked to a Southeast Asian pig-butchering / human-trafficking syndicate, after a DOJ investigation with OKX; largest USDT freeze at the time. DOJ simultaneously seized ~$9M.
Announced voluntary SDN freezing policy; froze 41 wallets controlled by OFAC-SDN-listed persons; 161 previously-listed addresses (~$3.5M USDT) blocked under the new policy.
Froze $181,000 USDT linked to the ~$1.5B Bybit hack (Lazarus Group) the day after the exploit.

Froze ~$27-28 million USDT on sanctioned Russian exchange Garantex, forcing it to halt operations; coordinated with a US/German/Finnish law-enforcement seizure of Garantex domains and servers announced 2025-03-07.
DOJ filed to seize the $225M frozen in the Nov 2023 pig-butchering case; described as the largest seizure in U.S. Secret Service history.
Participated with Chainalysis, Binance and OKX in an APAC law-enforcement operation freezing ~$47-50 million in pig-butchering funds.
Froze $182 million USDT across five TRON wallets tied to illicit activity.
Supported freeze of more than $344 million USDT across two addresses in coordination with OFAC and U.S. law enforcement; announcement cites cumulative $4.4B+ frozen.
On-chain trackers reported ~$515M USDT frozen across ~371 addresses on Ethereum and TRON in the preceding 30 days (aggregate of many actions, not a single event).
Froze the balances of all 131 ISIS-K TRON wallets named in the OFAC identifier update within hours of designation.

totals.metric: Blacklisted USDC addresses, third-party on-chain count

circle.policy: Reactive and judicially anchored: Circle states it denies access to addresses only to comply with applicable laws, regulations, or explicit court orders. CEO Jeremy Allaire reaffirmed in April 2026 that USDC will not be frozen without a court order.

documentedBlacklistEvents.event: Landmark: within the same news cycle as OFAC's Tornado Cash designation, Circle/Centre blacklisted the sanctioned Tornado Cash addresses (38 banned on Aug 8 per Centre; Dune counts cited 81 total banned addresses at the time), freezing ~75,000 USDC held across the 44 OFAC-listed Tornado addresses.

Froze three Ethereum wallets holding $63 million USDC tied to the July 2023 Multichain hack ($210M stolen overall) at the direction of the DOJ; a New York bankruptcy court later extended the freeze for Multichain liquidators.
Froze approximately $57 million USDC under a court order in litigation over the LIBRA memecoin scheme.
Froze 16 addresses (including a Goated.com wallet and an ICP bridge contract) in a civil case; after public criticism that the action was overbroad, unfroze one wallet (~130,966 USDC) on 2026-03-26.
CEO Jeremy Allaire publicly restated the court-order-only freeze policy amid criticism over delayed responses to thefts.

gaps.claim: Tornado Cash response asymmetry: OFAC designated Tornado Cash on 2022-08-08 and Circle blacklisted the sanctioned addresses within the same news cycle, but Tether publicly declined to proactively freeze the same addresses absent a law-enforcement request, and did not adopt any OFAC-SDN freezing policy until 2023-12-09 - roughly 16 months later.
gaps.evidence: Circle/Centre banned 38 addresses on Aug 8, 2022; Tether's Aug 2022 position was that it would not freeze Tornado addresses without instruction from authorities; Tether's voluntary SDN policy dates to Dec 1/9, 2023.

gaps.claim: Garantex enforcement lag of nearly three years: OFAC designated Garantex on 2022-04-05, yet the exchange kept operating and growing until the mass USDT freeze of 2025-03-06.
gaps.evidence: Garantex daily volumes grew more than 1,000% while under sanctions, from ~$11M/day (2022-03-01) to ~$121.6M/day (2025-03-01); the exchange only halted when Tether froze ~$27-28M USDT in coordination with a US/German/Finnish seizure of its infrastructure.

gaps.claim: Most Tether freezes have no corresponding OFAC designation: the OFAC SDN carries 93 USDT-tagged and 181 TRX-tagged address entries (mirror as of 2026-07-02), while third-party on-chain counts put Tether's blacklist at 7,268 addresses (as of 2025-10-07) - i.e., well over 90% of Tether-blacklisted addresses were frozen via law-enforcement requests, court orders, hack response, or Tether's own initiative rather than OFAC listing.
gaps.evidence: 928 total OFAC digital-currency address entries across all asset tags vs 7,268 Tether-blacklisted addresses; Tether's own framing cites 2,300+ law-enforcement cases across 65 countries, not sanctions lists.

gaps.claim: Issuer-vs-issuer scale gap: over 2023-2025 Tether blacklisted ~30x more addresses and ~30x more value than Circle (7,268 addresses / $3.29B vs 372 addresses / $109M), driven by Circle's court-order-only policy - meaning identical illicit flows are frozen if denominated in USDT but can keep moving in USDC until a court acts.
gaps.evidence: AMLBot/Dune snapshot 2025-10-07 gives the 30x differential; Circle CEO reaffirmed in April 2026 that USDC is not frozen without a court order 'even as hackers walk away with millions'.

gaps.claim: Freeze latency is exploitable: illicit actors have withdrawn approximately $78 million since 2017 during the window between a Tether freeze decision and its on-chain execution (multi-signature approval delay).
gaps.evidence: AMLBot's on-chain analysis of the gap between blacklist-submission and blacklist-execution transactions.

gaps.claim: eXch was never OFAC-designated despite laundering $200M+ of the Bybit/Lazarus hack: the takedown came from German-led law enforcement seizure, and the service shut itself down effective 2025-05-01 citing fear of an impending OFAC listing that never publicly materialized.
gaps.evidence: Elliptic documents the $200M+ Bybit laundering volume and eXch's 2025-03-31 statement about takedown attempts and possible OFAC listing; eXch does not appear in the SDN digital-currency address mirror.

gaps.claim: Designations can also outrun and then lag the courts: OFAC delisted Tornado Cash on 2025-03-21 after the Fifth Circuit's Van Loon ruling (2024-11-26) held that immutable smart contracts are not sanctionable 'property' - so for ~2.5 years the strictest enforcement (Circle's same-day blacklist) rested on a designation later withdrawn.
gaps.evidence: OFAC Recent Actions 2025-03-21 removal; Fifth Circuit ruling date and reasoning per Steptoe analysis.

gaps.claim: Counterpoint - the gap can close to hours when coordinated: on 2026-07-01 OFAC added 134 ISIS-K digital-asset identifiers and Tether froze all 131 TRON wallets within hours; but those wallets had already received over $1.4 million since 2023 and sent over $880,000 before designation, so the pre-designation window remains the dominant leak.
gaps.evidence: Chainalysis July 2026 analysis of the ISIS-K identifier update; BanklessTimes on the freeze timing.

coverageNotes: OFAC address counts come from the 0xB10C GitHub mirror (lists branch, last updated 2026-07-02T05:10:11Z), not directly from treasury.gov sdn.xml; the raw sdn.xml was not parsed in this pass, so any SDN changes between 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-12 are not reflected. Raw per-asset lists are archived locally in enforcement-gap/data/ofac_lists/.

The 928 'total address entries' figure sums per-asset-tag entries; cross-tag duplicates were checked only for ETH/USDT (4 shared) and TRX/USDT (0 shared), so the unique-address total is at most 924 but was not de-duplicated across all 18 tags.

Tether publishes no canonical machine-readable blacklist or official address count. The 7,268-address / $3.29B figure is a third-party on-chain count (AMLBot via Dune, snapshot 2025-10-07). Tether's own cumulative figure ($4.4B 'assets' frozen, 2026-04-23) includes non-USDT assets and law-enforcement cooperation beyond blacklisting; the two numbers are NOT directly comparable.
A widely-circulated '3,800+ addresses / $4.2B+' Tether figure appears in secondary blogs without clear provenance and was deliberately excluded.

Circle publishes no official blacklist count; the 372-address / $109M figure is third-party (AMLBot via Dune, snapshot 2025-10-07). Live Dune dashboards (dune.com/phabc/usdc-banned-addresses, dune.com/ozark/usdt-and-usdc-blacklist) are JS-rendered and could not be read without a browser, so no fresher count than 2025-10-07 was retrievable in this pass.
Could not confirm whether Circle removed the Tornado Cash addresses from the USDC blacklist after OFAC's 2025-03-21 delisting; no claim is made either way.
The May 2026 '371 addresses / ~$515M in 30 days' item is an aggregate reported by press from on-chain trackers, not a Tether announcement; exact window boundaries were not published.
The 2025-05 Circle LIBRA freeze (~$57M) is sourced to a single secondary page (a law firm's practice page); treat as lower-confidence than the other Circle events.
eXch's absence from OFAC lists was verified only against the mirror's digital-currency address lists, not the full SDN entity list.

No wallet addresses, per-hop flows, or intra-window dates were invented anywhere in this file; where a specific day was unavailable (e.g. '2025-06', '2025-08') only the granularity supported by sources is recorded.
